attackPath.dataflow: public signup -> owner-authenticated request -> recursive wildcard -> arbitrary nested storage
attackPath.reachability: Any public account can trigger the path; cross-account access is not required.

confidence.rationale: Static rules analysis and authenticated Emulator probes directly confirmed owner writes to unsupported nested paths.

preventiveControls: Review Firestore collection inventory whenever adapters add a domain.
findings.remediation: Replace the recursive wildcard with an explicit supported-collection allowlist, keep it one document deep, and add bounded schema validation for high-risk records.
remediationTests: Reject unsupported collection names and nested descendants.
Preserve reads of supported pre-Wave records.

rootCause.summary: The recursive wildcard treats user ownership as sufficient authorization for every unknown collection and descendant instead of limiting the supported data model.

severity.changeConditions: Lower if account creation becomes invite-only and independent per-user quotas are enforced.
severity.rationale: Public signup makes unsupported storage and subscribed-shape corruption deterministic; owner isolation limits confidentiality impact.

findings.summary: A public account can write arbitrary top-level and nested collections under its own user namespace because the recursive wildcard enforces ownership but no collection allowlist, depth bound, or schema validation.
findings.title: Owner wildcard permits unsupported Firestore schemas and nested storage

validation.evidence: The owner account could write arbitrary unsupported and nested documents; a second user remained denied.
validation.method: Static rules analysis plus authenticated Emulator probes.
validation.remainingUncertainty: Production billing limits were not observable.
validation.rubric: Public account reaches the write rule; schema and depth are unbounded.

attackPath.dataflow: public signup -> Firebase ID token -> planProjectWithAi -> OpenAI API
attackPath.reachability: Every public account satisfies the only identity check.

confidence.rationale: A direct static trace shows authentication followed by the paid provider sink with no authorization claim.

preventiveControls: Separate authentication and capability authorization for all cost-bearing Functions.
findings.remediation: Require a server-issued AI-access or operator custom claim before reading the provider secret or invoking the provider; add authorization regression tests.
remediationTests: Allow an account with the explicit server-issued claim.

rootCause.summary: Authentication is treated as authorization for a cost-bearing provider capability even though accounts are publicly creatable.

severity.changeConditions: Lower with a server-issued access claim plus per-UID quota or App Check.
severity.rationale: Low-skill authenticated abuse can consume paid quota and affect availability, while input limits and provider quotas cap individual requests.

findings.summary: The project-planning Function accepts any valid Firebase ID token from the public signup flow before making a paid OpenAI request; no entitlement, operator claim, App Check, or per-UID quota is enforced.
findings.title: Public accounts can invoke paid project-planning provider work

validation.evidence: verifyIdToken is followed by validation and provider invocation without an authorization decision.
validation.remainingUncertainty: Production quota and billing-alert configuration were unavailable.
validation.rubric: Public signup; paid sink; no role, entitlement, App Check, or per-UID quota.

attackPath.dataflow: workout text -> csvCell -> CSV download -> spreadsheet evaluation
attackPath.reachability: Any signed-in user can save workout text and export it.

confidence.rationale: Direct exporter invocation preserved every tested formula prefix.

preventiveControls: Use one shared spreadsheet-safe string encoder for future exports.
findings.remediation: Prefix dangerous string cells with an apostrophe after normalizing leading whitespace, and add regression coverage for every supported text column.
remediationTests: Neutralize formula prefixes, including after whitespace.

rootCause.summary: CSV quoting protects structure but does not neutralize spreadsheet interpretation of leading =, +, -, or @ after whitespace.

severity.changeConditions: Higher if third-party workout imports are later exported by a different operator.
severity.rationale: The consequence is meaningful but requires an explicit user export and downstream spreadsheet open, normally by the same account.

findings.summary: User-authored routine, exercise, and note text is quoted but formula prefixes remain executable when the downloaded CSV is opened in a spreadsheet.
findings.title: Workout CSV export does not neutralize spreadsheet formulas

validation.remainingUncertainty: Execution depends on the downstream spreadsheet.
validation.rubric: Attacker-influenced text reaches a spreadsheet cell without neutralization.

attackPath.dataflow: demo action -> global auth.currentUser -> ID token -> production Function
attackPath.reachability: Requires retained production authentication on localhost.

confidence.rationale: The source trace directly connects the demo action, persisted auth singleton, and production network sink without a demo guard.

preventiveControls: Pass explicit environment-scoped clients instead of reading global auth in domain helpers.
findings.remediation: Return before invoking the planner helper whenever demo mode is active, and lock source ordering with a regression test.
remediationTests: Assert the demo early return precedes requestProjectPlan.
Assert demo fixtures make no Firebase writes.

rootCause.summary: The route trusts synthetic context identity while its helper bypasses that context and consumes global Firebase authentication.

severity.changeConditions: Higher if production authentication is intentionally shared with demo sessions.
severity.rationale: A persisted production login on loopback plus an explicit planner action is required, but the path violates the promised zero-production-call demo boundary.

findings.summary: Demo context supplies a synthetic user, but the planner helper independently reads the persisted Firebase Auth singleton and targets a hard-coded production Function URL.
findings.title: Demo project planning can cross into the production Function

validation.evidence: The production request could occur before any demo-mode early return.
validation.rubric: Demo promise is synthetic; persisted production auth remains reachable.

attackPath.dataflow: legacy user record -> recursive sanitizer -> downloaded JSON
attackPath.reachability: Requires a credential-like field already stored and an explicit export.

confidence.rationale: Dynamic export tests emitted multiple credential-shaped fields unchanged.

preventiveControls: Prefer explicit per-domain export projections over generic object traversal.
findings.remediation: Expand the case-insensitive denylist and add nested-object regression fixtures for every excluded credential family.
remediationTests: Strip common token, session, cookie, private-key, and service-account names recursively.

rootCause.summary: The recursive sanitizer uses a narrow exact-key denylist that does not cover common credential and session names tolerated in legacy record shapes.

severity.changeConditions: Higher if integrations begin persisting opaque credential-bearing objects.
severity.rationale: Potential secret inclusion matters, but normal adapters do not write these fields and the export is explicitly user initiated.

findings.summary: The recursive export sanitizer promises credential exclusion but omits common field names such as token, idToken, authorization, clientSecret, session, cookie, privateKey, and serviceAccount.
findings.title: Whole-account export can include common credential-shaped fields

validation.evidence: token, idToken, authorization, clientSecret, session, and cookie survived export.
validation.method: Direct export invocation with credential-shaped fields.
validation.remainingUncertainty: Production records were intentionally not inspected.
validation.rubric: Tolerated records may carry legacy fields and the manifest promises exclusion.

attackPath.dataflow: authenticated account -> public acknowledgement fields -> provider operation
attackPath.reachability: Config-dependent and reachable by any account after enablement.

confidence.rationale: All gate inputs except ordinary Firebase authentication are client controlled or publicly documented.

preventiveControls: Document custom-claim provisioning and removal in deployment operations.
findings.remediation: Require an explicit operator custom claim in addition to the environment switch and acknowledgement.
remediationTests: Allow an account with the operator custom claim.

rootCause.summary: A static acknowledgement phrase is treated as operator authorization instead of requiring a server-issued identity attribute.

severity.changeConditions: Higher if provider enablement is broad or the response gains sensitive capabilities.
severity.rationale: The path is deterministic when enabled, but the feature is disabled by default and initially synthetic, reducing practical likelihood.

findings.summary: When the environment switch is enabled, any authenticated account can reproduce every client-supplied operator acknowledgement because no server-issued claim or UID policy distinguishes an operator.
findings.title: Assistant provider operator gate is a public static phrase

validation.evidence: Any authenticated account can reproduce the documented fields when enablement is true.
validation.method: Static authorization and request reproducibility analysis.
validation.rubric: Sensitive provider operation; public phrase; no server-issued operator identity.
